chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Faddal, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام asking him about a group of people among us who pray but do not fast in the month of Ramadan. Sometimes I need them to harvest for me, but when I call them for harvesting, they do not respond to me until I feed them, while they find others who feed them, so they go to them and leave me, and I am constrained from feeding them in the month of Ramadan.
So he عليه السلام wrote in his own hand: “I know it; feed them.”

key_terms.شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory time of fasting

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to feed non-fasting workers during the month of Ramadan when work depends on them?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the practical issue of hiring or relying on workers in Ramadan who do not fast and require food before working. Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام permits feeding them despite the discomfort felt about doing so during Ramadan. The narration reflects a legal and social ruling balancing religious sensitivity with livelihood needs.
